rationale:
agent_error_log.domain stores the empty string, not NULL, when a row has no domain. The consequence is that 'no domain' is unqueryable by the obvious predicate: measured 2026-08-08, `WHERE domain IS NULL` returned 128 rows out of 13,911 that have no domain (1.3%), and `count(domain)` counts '' as present. This is a reader-facing trap, not a cosmetic one: the tell is that it already misled this lane once (a `count(domain) = 160` reading, corrected in NOTES 3).

Until 2026-08-07 this was 3 outlier writers against 10 that wrapped the column in NULLIF, and the fix would have been 3 sites. RFC_012 B (f930de86b, 'the copy class is retired - 18 hand-copied agent_error_log INSERTs become one writer') consolidated the fleet onto agenterrors.Write, which carries the bare $2. That inverted the shape in both directions: '' is now produced fleet-wide by construction (measured: `domain IS NULL` returns 0 on every error_code written since the consolidation, where the guard codes previously produced NULL), and the fix collapsed to ONE line in the shared writer plus one in the single unconsolidated straggler.

Why the sibling NULLIF in the same INSERT is not evidence of intent, so the reviewer does not have to re-derive it: site_id and work_item_id are uuid columns and `SELECT ''::uuid` raises 'invalid input syntax for type uuid' (verified by running it). Their NULLIF is COMPELLED by the cast. domain is text, so nothing ever forced the question. The house convention is real and was followed elsewhere (32 `NULLIF($n,'')` uses on text columns across 24 files before the consolidation); domain was simply never brought into line.

This is submitted as a bug fix to a shared writer's stored shape, which is why it is here rather than committed quietly. It adds no capability, no new key, no new authority, and no branch: it makes an absent value store as SQL NULL, which is what every other absent column in the same INSERT already does.

plan.summary: Wrap agent_error_log.domain in NULLIF($n,'') at the two remaining INSERT sites, so an unset domain stores as SQL NULL rather than the empty string. One line each. No backfill, no reader change, no new config.

edits.rationale: The ONE writer since RFC_012 B; every consolidated caller (LogActionEntry, LogActionEntryFindings, orchestration.LogAgentError and the coordinator path) reaches the table through here, so this single line fixes all of them at once. Matches the NULLIF already applied to site_id and work_item_id in the same VALUES clause.

edits.rationale: A REGRESSION GUARD ONLY, and I want to be explicit that it cannot prove the behaviour. NULLIF is evaluated server-side, so sqlmock still observes the bind arg as '' - a mock cannot see a NULL that Postgres produces. The test therefore asserts the INSERT text wraps $2, which stops a future edit silently dropping it. The BEHAVIOURAL proof is the post-deploy live check in `risks`, not this test. Stating this rather than letting a green unit test imply more than it establishes.

plan.risks:
BLAST RADIUS MEASURED, NOT DELEGATED - this is the check I would otherwise be asking the reviewer to run.

1. Readers. Exactly one Go reader filters on this column: diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:269. Its behaviour is UNCHANGED by this edit, and the reason is the binding, not the predicate: nullText("") returns nil, so an unscoped diagnosis binds NULL and `$2::text IS NULL` short-circuits the whole clause; a scoped diagnosis binds a real domain, and rows carrying '' never matched a real domain before the change nor will NULL after it. The other three Go references to agent_error_log read `context` or are doc comments. A sweep of *.sql / *.sh / *.py / *.ts / *.tsx for `domain IS NULL`, `count(domain)` or `domain = ''` against this table returned ZERO hits. So no consumer's result set changes.

2. Consumers told, not merely measured (owner ruling 2026-07-29 item 3). The one affected consumer is the diagnosis loop's runtime tier (diagnose_load_runtime_action.go). What changes about its guarantee: nothing today; and after this, `domain IS NULL` becomes the correct way to ask 'unattributed' instead of silently returning 1.3% of them. Recorded in the lane's LANDMINES entry (footprints agent_error_log.domain, count(domain), domain IS NULL) which is synced into doc_notes, so seats and agents read it.

3. NO BACKFILL, deliberately, and named rather than omitted. 13,783 existing '' rows keep their value, so the table holds a MIXED shape indefinitely and `COALESCE(domain,'') = ''` remains the safe predicate for historical queries. Backfilling is a separate decision about rewriting history on a 18k-row table and is not smuggled in here. Note the population is also incident-driven (88% of the '' rows are one live vet-lane failure burst, 12,090 of 13,783 on 2026-08-04..08), so any argument from the row count is an argument about that incident, not about this defect - which is why the case above rests on the mechanism and the reader-side trap instead.

4. What this does NOT fix, stated so nobody inherits an overclaim: rows whose domain is genuinely unknown still carry no site attribution; this only makes their absence honestly representable. And it changes nothing about site_id.

5. VERIFICATION, and the unit test is not it. NULLIF is server-side, so sqlmock cannot observe the resulting NULL - the added test is a regression guard on the SQL text only. The behavioural proof is post-deploy at the artefact: after the roll, `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE domain IS NULL), count(*) FILTER (WHERE domain = '') FROM agent_error_log WHERE occurred_at > <roll>` must show the NULL bucket becoming non-zero for unset-domain rows and the '' bucket ceasing to grow. Per bugs_open/153 the image will also be pod-grepped for a string this change adds, with a deliberate misspelling as the discriminating negative control.
